tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file's content. Use search_files to locate relevant sections and offset+limit to read them. For large files, follow the returned nextRead cursor; range describes only the lines actually returned. Reuse unchanged content already in context instead of re-reading the same page. Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) are rendered as a compact cell listing for notebook_edit — pass raw:true for underlying JSON.

offset.description: 1-based line number to start reading from (omit to read from the top). Use with limit to page a large file.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return starting at offset (omit to read to end, subject to the size cap).

column.description: 1-based character position within the first rendered line. Use the column from nextRead to continue an oversized single line without repeating its beginning.

hashed.description: Prefix each line with a 6-char content hash for edit_file_hashed anchoring

raw.description: For .ipynb: return the raw notebook JSON instead of the rendered cell listing

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write content to a file (create or overwrite). For a large new file, write a small complete section first, then extend it with edit_file using a unique existing anchor. Aim for a few thousand characters of new content per call and wait for the result before continuing; each write_file call replaces the whole file.

path.description: Use exactly one listed canonical repo-relative path. Read tools may return absolute paths; those are not valid mutation arguments in this run. Do not use an absolute path, ./ prefix, .. segment or backslash. This schema is guidance; all execution-time permission and file-identity checks still apply.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace a string in a file. old_string must match EXACTLY ONE place — include enough surrounding context to make it unique, or the edit is rejected. To extend a file in small complete sections, use a unique existing anchor as old_string and retain that anchor plus the new section in new_string; do not resend the whole growing file. Wait for each edit result before continuing. Pass replace_all:true to change every occurrence instead.

path.description: Use exactly one listed canonical repo-relative path. Read tools may return absolute paths; those are not valid mutation arguments in this run. Do not use an absolute path, ./ prefix, .. segment or backslash. This schema is guidance; all execution-time permission and file-identity checks still apply.

old_string.description: Exact string to replace; must be unique in the file unless replace_all is true

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of old_string instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: edit_file_hashed
tools.description: Replace a single line in a file, anchored by its content hash. Use this instead of edit_file for robust edits: each line of read_file output (with hashed:true) is tagged with a 6-char hash like 'a3Kp9Z| const x = ...'. Pass the hash as anchor_hash, the current line as expected_line, and the replacement as new_line. Rejects edits if the line drifted (hash mismatch) — retry by re-reading the file with hashed:true.

path.description: Use exactly one listed canonical repo-relative path. Read tools may return absolute paths; those are not valid mutation arguments in this run. Do not use an absolute path, ./ prefix, .. segment or backslash. This schema is guidance; all execution-time permission and file-identity checks still apply.

anchor_hash.description: 6-char base64url hash of the line to replace (from read_file with hashed:true)

expected_line.description: Current content of the line — used as a second-layer check against hash collisions. Compared after .trim().

new_line.description: Replacement line content (without the hash tag prefix). Preserve the original indentation.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search for files by name pattern or content. For a long text file, pass path and pattern: returns matching line/column positions, nearby context, and nextRead arguments for read_file. This streams the file instead of loading it into model context. Continue capped results with nextOffset as offset. Omit path for the existing directory search.

path.description: One text file to search by literal keyword (takes precedence over directory/content_search).

regex.description: Single-file search only: evaluate a regular expression in overlapping 64K text windows (default false). Prefer literals for exact coverage across window boundaries.

caseSensitive.description: Single-file search only: match case (default false).

offset.description: Single-file search: zero-based character offset to continue from nextOffset (default 0).

contextChars.description: Single-file search: characters around each match (default 150).

content_search.description: If true, search file contents instead of names
